precepts.text: They mocked the messengers of God, despised his words and misused his prophets, until the wrath of the Lord arose, till there was no remedy.
precepts.point: They have thrown down thine altars and slain thy prophets, and I, even I only, am left. Israel's rulers killed the prophets who taught against them. The same people mock the purple and gold today.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Elijah cries that the children of Israel have “thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I, even I only, am left”. They made a covenant with death and hell. The prophets taught against the rulers and their falsehoods, so the rulers killed the prophets. Chronicles shows how it went all the way to the end of the kingdom.

“But they mocked the messengers of God”: that is what they do now. Look at how they mock the purple and gold, calling us purple Power Rangers. It is the same thing; they mocked us. “and despised his words”: despised his law, like they do now. “and misused his prophets”: had them locked up, exiled, or killed in terrible ways.

“until the wrath of the Lord arose against his people, till there was no remedy.” They pissed the Lord off until there was no remedy left. The killing of the prophets Elijah complained of was not one king’s sin; it was the way of the nation until the wrath came.

precepts.text: They mocked the messengers of God and misused his prophets, till there was no remedy.
precepts.point: They are drunken, but not with wine; the Lord hath closed your eyes, the prophets and seers hath he covered.

note.label: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

precepts.why:
Why did the Lord cover the eyes of the prophets and rulers? “But they mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words, and misused his prophets, until the wrath of the Lord arose against his people, till there was no remedy.”

Ezra says the same: “I sent unto you my servants the prophets, whom ye have taken and slain, and torn their bodies in pieces, whose blood I will require of your hands”. We tortured our prophets, killed them, and tore them in pieces.

Stephen told the rulers of his time, “as your fathers did, so do ye. Which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted? and they have slain them which shewed before of the coming of the Just One”. The Pharisees and the builders of that time were the children of the murderers of the prophets who prophesied of Christ. Their fathers killed the prophets who spoke of him, and then they were born and killed Christ himself. They have always hated him, from their fathers to them. When Stephen reminded them, “they were cut to the heart”, because they knew, and they gnashed on him and killed him.

So the darkness of Isaiah 29 did not fall without cause. They mocked, despised and misused, until there was no remedy, and the Lord poured out on them the spirit of deep sleep.

precepts.text: As the ruler is, so are his people, and the power of the earth is in the hand of the Most High, who sets over it one that is profitable in due time.
precepts.point: The power of the earth is in the hand of the Most High, and in due time he sets over it one that is profitable. When Israel will not rule in righteousness, he raises a Nebuchadnezzar; Israel's purpose was never to be wicked and rule at the same time.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

precepts.why:
“A wise judge will instruct his people; and the government of a prudent man is well ordered. As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers; and what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein. An unwise king destroyeth his people”. As the ruler is, so are his people.

Jehoiakim “did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord his God”, and he destroyed his people. “Against him came up Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and bound him in fetters, to carry him to Babylon.” Nebuchadnezzar “also carried of the vessels of the house of the Lord to Babylon, and put them in his temple at Babylon.”

“The power of the earth is in the hand of the Lord, and in due time he will set over it one that is profitable.” The Most High set a wicked king over the land because his own people would not do what he said. When Israel will not rule in righteousness, he raises a Nebuchadnezzar. Israel’s purpose was never to be wicked and rule at the same time.

precepts.text: When the wickedness of man was great and every imagination of his heart only evil, the Most High grieved and purposed to destroy man from the face of the earth; a repeated pattern of evil brings his judgment.
precepts.point: The Most High sends to them by his messengers, rising up early and sending because he had compassion, but they mock the messengers, despise his words, and misuse his prophets until the wrath of the Lord arises and there is no remedy.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

precepts.why:
The Most High “saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” It grieved him at his heart, and he said, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth.”

That is the pattern behind the fall of Jerusalem. Zedekiah did evil in the sight of the Lord his God, humbled not himself before Jeremiah the prophet, stiffened his neck and hardened his heart. The chief of the priests and the people transgressed very much after all the abominations of the heathen and polluted the house of the Lord.

A repeated pattern of evil brings his judgment. The Most High sent his messengers, rising up betimes, because he had compassion; but they mocked the messengers, despised his words and misused his prophets, “until the wrath of the Lord arose against his people, till there was no remedy.” As in the days before the flood, when the wickedness is great and continual, destruction comes.

precepts.text: What comes into the mind to be as the heathen serving wood and stone shall not be, for the Most High rules with a mighty hand and fury poured out until his people acknowledge him.
precepts.point: The Most High sends to them by his messengers, rising up early and sending because he had compassion, but they mock the messengers, despise his words, and misuse his prophets until the wrath of the Lord arises and there is no remedy.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

precepts.why:
Israel said in their mind, “We will be as the heathen, as the families of the countries, to serve wood and stone.” The Most High answers, “that which cometh into your mind shall not be at all.”

That is what the chief of the priests and the people did in Zedekiah’s days: they “transgressed very much after all the abominations of the heathen.” They wanted to be like the nations. But he will not let his people become the heathen: “As I live, saith the Lord God, surely with a mighty hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with fury poured out, will I rule over you.”

So the wrath that arose against his people, till there was no remedy, is that fury poured out. The Most High rules over Israel with a mighty hand until his people acknowledge him.

precepts.point: They burn the house of God, break down the walls of Jerusalem, burn its palaces, and destroy all the goodly vessels, exactly the fierce nation the curses warned of.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

precepts.why:
The curses of the law said it before it happened: “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth; a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand; A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young.”

That nation is the king of the Chaldees. He slew their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary, and “had no compassion upon young man or maiden, old man, or him that stooped for age.” No regard for the old, no favour to the young, exactly as written.

The Most High gave them all into Nebuchadnezzar’s hand. The vessels of the house of God, the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king and his princes, were brought to Babylon; the house of God was burnt and the wall of Jerusalem broken down. This is the fierce nation the curses warned of, come upon Judah.

precepts.text: The Most High will plead for his heritage Israel whom the nations scattered and parted his land, casting lots for his people and selling them, and he will return their recompense on their own heads.
precepts.point: They burn the house of God, break down the walls of Jerusalem, burn its palaces, and destroy all the goodly vessels, exactly the fierce nation the curses warned of.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

precepts.why:
The same Most High who gave Judah into the hand of the Chaldees will plead for them. “I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land.”

The nations “have cast lots for my people; and have given a boy for an harlot, and sold a girl for wine.” They took his silver and his gold and “carried into your temples my goodly pleasant things”, just as all the vessels and treasures of the house of the Lord were carried to Babylon. And “The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians, that ye might remove them far from their border.”

So the carrying away is not the end of the matter. The nations that scattered Israel, parted his land and sold his people will be judged: “swiftly and speedily will I return your recompence upon your own head.”

precepts.text: He sent to them by his messengers because he had compassion on his people, but they mocked the messengers and misused his prophets, until there was no remedy.
precepts.point: This is repetitive through the whole history. Any time the Most High sends a prophet to warn his people about destruction, that is compassion, because he did not have to do it.

note.label: Zechariah 1: Turn Ye Unto Me, and I Will Turn Unto You

precepts.why:
Be ye not as your fathers, unto whom the former prophets have cried. This is repetitive through the whole history. “And the Lord God of their fathers sent to them by his messengers, rising up betimes, and sending; because he had compassion on his people, and on his dwelling place”.

Any time the Most High sends a prophet to warn his people about destruction, that is compassion, because he did not have to do it. “But they mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words, and misused his prophets, until the wrath of the Lord arose against his people, till there was no remedy.” That is why he was sore displeased with our fathers: they did not hear, nor hearken, until there was no remedy. Turn ye unto me, and I will turn unto you, is that same compassion offered again.

note.label: Spiritual Uprising: When God Shakes a Nation

precepts.why:
“Jehoiakim was twenty and five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem”. He did evil in God's sight. “Against him came up Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon”. God used Nebuchadnezzar the Babylonian to take down the southern kingdom. “and bound him in fetters, to carry him to Babylon.” Both kingdoms went down because all of us were evil. The northern kingdom had idols; so did the southern kingdom. That's still what you see in black churches today.

The chief priests and people transgressed after the heathen's abominations and polluted the Lord's house. “And the Lord God of their fathers sent to them by his messengers”. God sent prophets to warn the southern kingdom because he had compassion on his people. “But they mocked the messengers of God, and despised his words”. They mocked the prophets. It's the same when we're in the streets today. In front of 2819 church, they mocked us: the Israelites are always yelling and screaming. There's no difference. We're the most rebellious people.
